note: A quirk is a fact about the world the PC was given, so it cuts both ways and a run may carry any number (section 1). SPEC section 6.1 unlocks none at game start. The file exists so that adding one is adding an entry rather than adding a file, which is the whole point of the framework. Every magnitude here is tuning and belongs to M8 (section 6): the code knows how to turn the knobs an entry names and knows nothing about how far.

entries.name: Scarce iron
entries.blurb: The Crown's ironmongers name a shocking figure, and the hills here are miserly.
entries.note: The asymmetry is the whole quirk (section 4). The Crown's price rises far more than the ore yield falls, so buying your way out stops working and the way out is your own foundry - the mineworks, the ore, the chain buildings.md section 5 already makes the spine of construction. It makes the tool wall sharper, the gunsmith gate a genuine prize, and the natives, who covet exactly these three, a much more serious trading partner. Placeholders: the gap between the two figures is the entire quirk and M8 owns it.

entries.name: Commando commanders
entries.blurb: The men the Marshal spares you have seen a great deal, and expect to see more.
entries.note: Commanders begin with a level or two and the survival coin flip is harsher (section 4). Rewards using them well; punishes losing them, which is mostly not in your hands. commanders.md section 7 already says the flip need not be even. Placeholders: both figures are M8's.

entries.name: Busy patrons
entries.blurb: Word of the colony has got about at court, and everyone has a proposal.
entries.note: More arrive and each is easier to please, against more hands out and more of the desk (section 4). Rewards a player who works the patron game; drowns one who ignores it. The drawback is not bolted on - it is the letters themselves, and SPEC section 9.6's volume is the real constraint. Two knobs, because the count alone does nothing: DemandSchedule's reach ceiling is what actually caps arrivals, and demands.json records that the last three of those seven hands are the three patrons. So more patrons means more hands out, which is also the drawback stated honestly. The 'easier to please' half waits on a per-role drift knob, which the clergy ticket (#277) brings.

entries.name: A pious colony
entries.blurb: They came for the freedom to worship, and they have not forgotten it.
entries.note: Clergy carry higher prominence everywhere, so churches matter more in BOTH directions - a contented priest holds his town down harder and a slighted one carries it out faster. And amusement contributes less pleasure, because they disapprove. Rewards investing in faith; punishes bread and circuses, which closes off quality-of-life.md section 8's rum trap from the other end. Both figures are tuning.

entries.name: It could be worse
entries.blurb: Whatever befalls this colony, somebody here has seen worse and says so.
entries.note: Everything that measures quality of life does so with a dampened effect (section 4). It flattens the curve in BOTH directions: misery hurts less, so less rebel sentiment, fewer complaints and a steadier colony; comfort helps less, so weaker immigration appeal, slower births and less of the virtuous circle. Rewards a player who never meant to invest in how people live; punishes one whose whole plan was to make the colony pleasant. One knob rather than two, because one measure feeds every reader - the damper contracts the measure toward the middle of its range and each reader goes on reading it exactly as it always did. Section 5 names this with Boom town as the pair to watch: one raises the pressure and the other numbs the feedback. The magnitude is M8's.

entries.name: Boom town
entries.blurb: Every ship brings more of them, and they all mean to stay.
entries.note: Immigration runs higher and the stakes multiplier on rebel sentiment runs higher with it (section 4). This is immigration.md section 9's chain - growth is the engine of prosperity and the engine of rebellion at once - made into a choice. A player who can hold a large colony gets a larger one sooner; a player who cannot gets to the cliff faster. The drawback is not bolted on, it is the same sentence as the benefit. The stakes knob scales a figure that is already capped, and rebel_sentiment.gd records why that cap is load-bearing: both magnitudes are M8's and neither should be moved without the harness.

entries.name: Restless country
entries.blurb: The people here have met Europeans before, and they are ready for you.
entries.note: The tribes are stronger, not merely grumpier (section 4). They start at lower standing, their villages yield more from the tiles they work, their forces are more numerous, and their trade agreements are richer. So the escape from the Crown's monopoly (natives.md section 5) is both more valuable and harder to reach, and a colony that mishandles its neighbours faces something that can actually take a town. Four knobs for four bullets. The richer agreements are volume and never the ratio: natives.md section 5 fixes that each side receives at fair value, so what a richer agreement means is that a people who get more off their land put more of it on the table and still keep the winter. Every figure is M8's.

entries.name: Distant colony
entries.blurb: Six weeks of open water, and every question you ask is answered by a man who has stopped waiting for it.
entries.note: Correspondence takes an extra month each way (section 4), and this is the only quirk that changes the LOOP rather than a magnitude inside it - which is why section 7 said it wanted its knob designed deliberately and why it took three. post_crossing is one number read by both directions, because 'each way' means the same delay each way: two numbers would let a run exist where the PC hears late and is obeyed promptly, which is a slow contact rather than a distant colony. The inbound half is a QUEUE and not a delay on delivery - a held letter says what was true the month it was written, because InboundLetter is already a snapshot. The other two are the compensation section 4 promises: contacts are more patient, so silence costs less and their dampers run longer, and the desk is thinner for it. You manage less and plan further, which is a different game rather than a harder one. Every figure is M8's, and section 6 flags the crossing length as the one that decides whether the loop still reads as correspondence or starts reading as delay.
